newsitem.title: QATAR: U.N. plans Mideast forum to fight drug abuse.
newsitem.headline: U.N. plans Mideast forum to fight drug abuse.

text.p: The United Nations, fighting rising narcotics abuse in the Middle East, is planning a regional forum next year to promote cooperation in the war on drugs, U.N. officials said on Sunday.

"This forum will bring together people from the ministries of education, social affairs, health...and provide the region with an arena for exchange of information and experiences (with drug abuse)," said Peter Storr, chief of technical services of the U.N. Drug Control Programme (UNDCP).

"We hope to be able to organise this (drug) demand reduction forum in the Middle East early next year", he told an international conference on the "Fight Against Drugs", sponsored by Interpol and Qatar's ministry of interior.
Storr said the flourishing global drug trade was worth up to $500 billion annually, making it the second largest business after the arms trade.

"Identifiable costs of drug abuse in consumer countries seem to range from 0.5 to 1.3 percent of gross domestic product, the largest part of which involves drug-related crime and law enforcement costs," he said.

Storr said Middle East drug abuse centred on the stimulant fenetylline, commonly known under the brand name Captagon. The smuggling of significant quantities of illicitly manufactured fenetylline from Europe was continuing, he said.

"Despite all our efforts, the problem of drug abuse seems to be growing," Storr said. "But the good news is that we can see a growing commitment of countries and international organisations to tackle the problem together."
